selection_reasoning: This forms a natural 3-step dependency chain. The player must first climb a ladder to reach an elevated platform where the diamond block is placed (making it inaccessible without climbing). Once on the platform, they find and mine the diamond block to obtain diamonds. Finally, they use those diamonds along with sticks (which can be provided on the platform or via a crafting table with wood) to craft a diamond sword. Each task logically depends on the previous one, creating a coherent multi-hop challenge.

milestones.description: Uses position_inside_box because this is a movement/navigation task — the player must physically climb the ladder to reach the elevated platform. The platform is at y=4 (spawn-relative), so standing on it puts the player at y≈5. The box covers the platform footprint (0,3)-(8,10) in XZ with generous margins, and y range 5-8 to confirm the player is on the elevated surface. Only reachable via the ladder in this scene.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task — the player must navigate near the diamond block and look at it to confirm visual discovery. The diamond block is at spawn-relative (5, 5, 7) on top of the platform. max_distance=8 allows detection from anywhere on the ~8x7 block platform. facing_tolerance=60 ensures the player is actually looking toward the diamond block, not just standing nearby.

Uses inventory_has because crafting a diamond sword results in the item appearing in the player's inventory. The player starts with 2 diamonds and 1 stick (no diamond_sword), so the only way to satisfy min_count=1 is by successfully crafting at the crafting table on the platform. This is the preferred rule type for craft tasks.
